why: FAMES applied to FAMES. A case is one deterministic, zero-model, re-runnable probe that states its expectation before it runs (FP), costs one script invocation and no tokens (MTM), charges its failure to a named residual dimension (SCF), makes a non-zero residual the only change trigger (AEX), and is replayable from a record citing package_sha (SEAL). Adding a check means adding data here, not adding code.

C-CAPABILITY-COMPLETE reads hand-written flags, so it can only count claims, never test them -- X6 read implemented=true for weeks while run() had no caller at all. This case makes the ledger falsifiable: every stage flagged implemented must write its own status row in the engine. Closed, because a ledger that overstates the code is worse than one that admits a gap. NOT_APPLICABLE on a seat that has no acquire.py.

acquisition_is_never_a_model_job as a probe instead of as prose. Every row in this file's own capability map is an acquire.* capability -- the model-consuming ones (asr, vision, text) are inherited by reference under one-writer-per-provider-list and are not written here -- so a true value means a model was placed on the path that turns a URL into raw bits, which is exactly what the rule forbids. It is also the enforceable half of model_output_as_query: a model may say WHERE to look only because the fetch that follows is deterministic and measured downstream. Closed, because a model inside acquisition makes every fact after it unmeasured. Known limit, stated rather than hidden: a capability row that omits needs_model entirely is not caught, because a wildcard pointer collects only the values that resolve -- the same gap C-CAPABILITY-DECLARED carries for stages. Catching an absent key needs a new case kind, which is code, so it is recorded as residual instead of being faked here.

a convergence path that nobody measures is indistinguishable from a dead one: the seat looks green on its last known generation while its clock has not fired for days. Every converge run stamps this heartbeat, so an absent or stale file IS the residual. Degraded, because a machine that is simply switched off is honestly behind rather than broken, and 6h tolerates sleep while still catching a runner that died within a working day.

the runner must be a registered rider on this seat's own clock, not a command someone remembers to type. The heartbeat records what the seat measured about its own registration, so drift (a moved workspace, a changed cadence) and a seat with no clock at all both surface here instead of silently degrading to manual convergence.

an unmeasured runtime host is assumed healthy, and on 2026-08-17 that assumption cost 48 minutes: an AppX repair finished its Add step, failed its Register step, and left the package Modified/NeedsRemediation while the app still launched, so nothing looked wrong until work started failing. A read-only check already existed and no clock called it. The tick stamps this heartbeat, so an absent or stale file IS the residual -- without it a dead prober and a healthy machine are the same picture. 6h matches C-CONVERGE-HEARTBEAT rather than the 5m cadence, because this ceiling only detects a dead prober; real detection latency for a broken package is the rider's own cadence. Degraded, because a powered-off machine is honestly behind rather than broken.

the seat's capacity to execute at all is a capability, and a package carrying no Trust Label after a half-completed repair still starts, still opens a window, and still fails at the first packaged-service call. Health is taken from the repair tool's own -CheckOnly verdict rather than from a predicate reimplemented here, so this probe asks exactly the question its consumer asks; a parse that disagrees with the tool's exit code writes unknown instead of outvoting the instrument, and unknown is not in range so it reddens here too. Degraded rather than closed on purpose: a corrupt host must be loud, but blocking every run would also block the run that repairs it.

the tick re-reads hosts.json after it runs, so this is the registry's answer and not the engine's exit code. It stays red until the operator arms the rider, which is the correct picture rather than a defect to hide: arming a schedule is the operator's authority, so an agent that proposed one and an operator who accepted one must be distinguishable. It also catches a rider later removed or renamed, where the heartbeat would otherwise keep arriving from a hand-run command and read as an armed clock.
